item.subject: science
item.stem:
The teacher writes one answer on the board: "three". Pupils must invent a curious situation and a scientific question that this answer could fit. Ideas mentioned include wet handkerchiefs, leaves changing colour, and space.

Which response best follows the activity?

options.A: She imagines three wet handkerchiefs drying at different speeds and asks which factors could explain the differences.
options.B: She asks, "Why do leaves change colour?" without checking whether "three" answers that question.
options.C: She says a scientific question is valid only when its answer is already known, so the activity is impossible.
options.D: She writes any long, dramatic question about space and says it is valid because it sounds creative, even though "three" does not answer it.
